correctness.rationale: The graph moment expansion is exact by Walsh orthogonality and enumeration of 4-cycles. Two Cauchy--Schwarz bounds (pairwise-products and mixed-bottom-row) rigorously show that columnwise and rowwise root-mean-square symmetrization preserves coefficient \(\ell_2\) energy and never decreases the fourth moment. The three-block reduction has exact concave normalized expression with strict interior maximizer and exact quadratic deficit; its achieved value is the claimed rational sharp constant. Strict equality and 4-cycle sign constraints yield all extremizers. The all-dimensions argument covers \(n\ge2\) including tree boundary \(n=2\); the embedded exact verifier was replayed successfully and its finite diagnostics are not treated as proof.

originality.rationale: The accessible original bilinear-moment paper treats moments of unweighted complete ordinary/decoupled bilinear forms while optimizing the marginal laws, not an arbitrary real coefficient array with one fixed omitted interaction. Pairwise-independent-sign results vary the random-vector law, and fourth-moment-theorem results address normal approximation. Ordinary full-support finite-dimensional Khintchine tensorization yields the weaker \((3-2/n)^2\) ratio. The new restriction has a distinct exact \(C_n\), two-level extremizers and an exact deletion loss. Indexed published-result searches of support, alias and rational-formula variants returned no implication-equivalent covering theorem; absence of indexed hits is not itself novelty proof.

value.rationale: The punctured product of first-order Rademacher subspaces is a canonical finite-dimensional Banach-function-space inclusion. A single deleted interaction forces a nontrivial exact norm decrement relative to the full tensor product, with closed formula for every dimension, an exact \(n^{-2}\) asymptotic loss, and a complete two-level extremizer classification. This is a natural missing-interaction robustness invariant rather than a generic simple substitution, a known-table recomputation or an arbitrary numerical slice. The value claim is limited to the stated real fourth-moment setting.
